South Alabama Jaguars.oc: Major Applewhite himself — the guide records he will call the offense. Rob Ezell left for Wake Forest after 2024 and Paul Petrino held the role last season.
South Alabama Jaguars.dc: Todd Orlando, whom the guide calls a football lifer hired to fix the defense.
South Alabama Jaguars.oc_status: New — the guide records Applewhite taking the play-calling himself, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
South Alabama Jaguars.dc_status: The guide states this two ways — see the conflicts field. The team pages (pp. 340–341) record Applewhite hiring Todd Orlando to fix the defense, while the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
South Alabama Jaguars.play_caller: Major Applewhite, explicitly — the guide reads it as one of two staffing decisions showing he knows things need to improve.
South Alabama Jaguars.offensive_scheme: Not named, but the guide sets out what Applewhite is chasing using explosive-play data from BCF Toys: under Paul Petrino, South Alabama ranked 88th in share of plays gaining 7-plus yards and 124th at 10-plus; under Rob Ezell, 24th and 54th.
South Alabama Jaguars.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records that even the 2024 defense allowed 5.8 yards per play while conceding 25.2 points per game — already a big drop from the two seasons before that under head coach Kane Wommack.
South Alabama Jaguars.tempo: Expected to rise. Lacking size at receiver, the guide expects Applewhite to run more tempo to use that group's speed and get the ball out quickly into space.
South Alabama Jaguars.run_pass: Expected to shift. With 1,000-yard rusher Kentrell Bullock gone from a run-reliant offense built around him, the guide expects Bishop Davenport to be asked to throw and run more.
South Alabama Jaguars.personnel: Addressed as a size limitation at receiver.
South Alabama Jaguars.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide is positive on Davenport — he prepared all summer knowing the team is his and completed 68% of his passes with a 12-to-6 ratio — and records in fairness to the coach that Applewhite expected Gio Lopez back until North Carolina arrived with money after spring practices.
South Alabama Jaguars.continuity: Head coach and quarterback return; the offensive coordinator changes with the head coach absorbing the role. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 0, 3 and 4, plus 1 for 8 returning starters, totalling 12. The team pages describe the defensive coordinator position differently — see the conflicts field.
South Alabama Jaguars.staff_turnover: The guide traces a coordinator carousel: Rob Ezell left for the same job at Wake Forest after a 2024 season in which the Jaguars posted 6.8 yards per play and surrendered only 17 sacks; Paul Petrino could not sustain those numbers, though the guide grants he got a raw deal with Lopez leaving; and Applewhite has now taken the offense himself and brought in Todd Orlando.
South Alabama Jaguars.prior_school: Wake Forest is where Ezell went. On the roster the guide records Nehemiah Chandler leaving for Florida State and Gio Lopez for North Carolina.
South Alabama Jaguars.portal_recruiting: A split verdict. The guide records the fourth-ranked freshman class per 247Sports alongside the second-worst transfer portal class, states surprise that the Jaguars did not pursue portal receivers with more fervour, and calls the defense completely rebuilt with limited portal help.
South Alabama Jaguars.vsin_assessment: A rubber match, with the coach's own decisions read as the evidence. The guide grades year one a win — 7-6 with 6.8 yards per play, a full yard per play better than opponents, and 34.4 points — and year two a major disappointment at 4-8 with 5.4 yards per play and 26.5 points alongside defensive regression. It is explicit that it does not think Applewhite's job is in jeopardy even with another poor showing, while noting he knows things need to improve, which it reads in two staffing decisions: calling the offense himself and hiring Todd Orlando.
South Alabama Jaguars.strengths: A head coach with a documented strong first season taking back play-calling, a returning quarterback who completed 68% of his passes and knows the job is his, the fourth-ranked freshman class nationally, and a veteran coordinator brought in for the defense.
South Alabama Jaguars.concerns: The second-worst transfer portal class, the loss of a 1,000-yard rusher and a receiver whose 67 catches were 27 more than anyone else's, a defense with the top four tacklers gone and nobody on the team having reached two sacks, and thin depth with a very green secondary.
South Alabama Jaguars.betting: The guide attaches an unusually strong variance warning: this is as high-variance a team as you will see in the Sun Belt. Faster tempo and explosive plays would change the story, but could also hurt a team very short on depth and very green in the secondary.
South Alabama Jaguars.conflicts: The guide states the defensive coordinator position two ways. The team pages (pp. 340–341) record that Major Applewhite has hired football lifer Todd Orlando to fix the defense, while the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator. Both are reproduced as printed and neither is corrected.

Southern Miss Golden Eagles.previous_hc_experience: Extensive, and the Coaching Carousel gives both sides. Blake Anderson has a decade of FBS coaching experience, took Arkansas State to new heights from 2014-20 and had an 11-win season at Utah State to start his tenure there, but also had an unceremonious departure from Utah State and did not coach in 2024. The team pages state the circumstances: he was fired from Utah State over allegations that he improperly reported instances of sexual misconduct under university rules, in a case that also cost the deputy athletic director their job.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.oc: Not addressed by name for 2026. Anderson himself held the role last season.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.dc: Joe Bolden, who has never held the position before.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator, the role Anderson vacated on becoming head coach.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.dc_status: New — the guide records Bolden taking over, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide's expectation is deflationary — the Golden Eagles threw for 266 yards per game last season, their most since 2019, and it says not to expect anything like that again.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Landry Lyddy staying after 406 yards with a 2-to-3 ratio and allows the possibility he was merely stuck behind Braylon Braxton, and notes Anderson's addition Ethan Hampton started a few games at Northern Illinois but barely played for Illinois.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.continuity: None. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator, 0 for the quarterback and 0 for a single returning starter — a total of 0.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.staff_turnover: Complete, and internal. Charles Huff left for Memphis and the Golden Eagles opted to keep it in-house by elevating Anderson from offensive coordinator, with a first-time coordinator taking the defense.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.prior_school: Arkansas State and Utah State for Anderson; Michigan, Ohio State, Nevada, Tulsa and Southern Miss itself for Joe Bolden, whose varied path the guide lists while noting he has not stayed long anywhere and admitting it is unsure what to make of that. On the roster it records Ethan Hampton from Illinois by way of Northern Illinois.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.portal_recruiting: The whole roster, and the guide quantifies the loss precisely: 20 players had at least 20 tackles last season and 19 of them are playing elsewhere or not at all, while all nine players with at least 15 receptions are outside the programme, leaving a hodgepodge of transfers and holdovers who stayed knowing jobs were available. It explains the mechanism — many players went to Memphis with Huff or simply wanted to play their final season for him.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.vsin_assessment: An uninspiring promotion by the Carousel's reckoning, and a baseline the team pages say was weaker than the record. The Coaching Carousel records the elevation, notes the Utah State departure, calls this a fairly uninspiring hire in Hattiesburg, and adds that Anderson has won at both stops and has done so while navigating some very difficult and tragic family circumstances, so we'll see how this stop goes. The team pages describe last season as catching lightning in a bottle, record the production case for the promotion — the offense improved by 13.5 points and a full yard per play on Anderson's watch — then argue the 7-6 record overstated the team: only +18 in point differential and +0.3 in yards per play, out-gained on a per-carry basis, and heavily helped by a +14 turnover margin, a combination it calls hard to believe. Its conclusion is carefully worded: not that this team will be better, but that last year's team was not that good.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.strengths: A head coach with a decade of FBS experience, a programme high-water mark at Arkansas State and an 11-win season at Utah State, and a documented offensive improvement of 13.5 points and a full yard per play in the role he just left.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.concerns: A Stability Score of 0 with a single returning starter, 19 of the 20 players with at least 20 tackles gone and all nine players with at least 15 receptions outside the programme, a first-time defensive coordinator, and what the guide calls serious recipe-for-disaster potential in combining a great many JUCO and FCS transfers with that coordinator.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.betting: The guide's coaching-adjacent market record is that Southern Miss lost twice as a favourite over the final three games and also lost as a pick 'em and at +1.
Southern Miss Golden Eagles.carousel_summary: Adam Burke records the sequence plainly: Anderson's second stint at Southern Miss was to serve as the OC and QB coach, but Charles Huff left for Memphis and the Golden Eagles opted to keep it in-house with Anderson. He weighs the résumé from both directions — a decade of FBS coaching experience, but also an unceremonious departure from Utah State and no coaching in 2024; Arkansas State taken to new heights from 2014-20 and an 11-win season at Utah State to start that tenure. His verdict is that this is a fairly uninspiring hire in Hattiesburg. He closes on the human side: Anderson has won at both stops and has done so while navigating some very difficult and tragic family circumstances, so we'll see how this stop goes.

Troy Trojans.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed as a head coach. The guide records Gerad Parker as the former Notre Dame coordinator who had been offensive coordinator at West Virginia under former Trojans head coach Neal Brown — which it says is why he appealed to Troy.
Troy Trojans.oc_status: New — the guide records Austin's arrival, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Troy Trojans.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Troy Trojans.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Troy Trojans.offensive_scheme: Not named, but characterised by the coordinator's output: Adam Austin led a Tarleton offense with five 50-point games that was the highest-scoring team at the FCS level and second only to North Texas across all of Division I.
Troy Trojans.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Dontae Wright's measurable year-over-year gains — 28.4 points per game in 2024 down to 23.9, more than 6% shaved off opponents' completion percentage, 18 more sacks and 0.4 fewer yards per play allowed.
Troy Trojans.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records just 2.8 yards per carry, the worst offensive season since the Larry Blakeney era.
Troy Trojans.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide treats the Tucker Kilcrease–Goose Crowder situation as a rarity in the transfer era — two quarterbacks who both stayed — traces the injury sequence, and draws its evidence on their relative standing from the market: when Crowder was hurt and Kilcrease took over, the betting action indicated Kilcrease was seen as a clear downgrade.
Troy Trojans.continuity: Head coach, defensive coordinator and quarterback return; the offensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 0, 3 and 4, plus 0 for 6 returning starters, totalling 11.
Troy Trojans.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator per the Stability Score table.
Troy Trojans.prior_school: Notre Dame and West Virginia for Parker, with the West Virginia link to Neal Brown given as the reason Troy hired him. Tarleton for Adam Austin. On the roster the guide notes a number of East Mississippi CC players including 6-foot-5 quarterback Rodge Waldrop.
Troy Trojans.portal_recruiting: Credited as a staff strength by inference. The guide's inference from the 2024-to-2025 defensive improvement is that this staff is adept at finding talent in the portal, and it records the portal heavily used to fill out the offensive line.
Troy Trojans.vsin_assessment: Among the nation's top coaching jobs, in the guide's own words. It rates Parker's four-win improvement that highly given cluster injuries on the offensive line and at quarterback, while putting the raw number in perspective — 8-6 does not stand out, especially with Jon Sumrall having gone 23-5 before leaving for Tulane. It describes last season as winning ugly: 59 sacks allowed, which it stresses it verified as not a typo and seven more than the next closest team, and a 6-3 conference record while being out-gained by nearly a full yard per play. Its closing case is health-based: Parker reached eight wins with what it calls a dumpster fire on the offensive line and two injured quarterbacks, the roster is better now, and it cannot imagine the health luck being that bad again.
Troy Trojans.strengths: A head coach the guide rates as having done one of the nation's top coaching jobs, a coordinator hire from the highest-scoring offense at the FCS level, a defensive coordinator with measurable gains across points, completion percentage, sacks and yards per play, two quarterbacks who both stayed, and a staff the guide infers is adept in the portal.
Troy Trojans.concerns: 59 sacks allowed — seven more than the next closest team — with a couple of returning line starters the guide does not treat as automatically good news, 2.8 yards per carry, only six returning starters, and essentially all of the top defensive players gone apart from an 11-sack edge.
Troy Trojans.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching, though its market observation about the quarterbacks — that betting action treated Kilcrease as a clear downgrade — is coaching-adjacent.

ULM Warhawks.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records Bryant Vincent's career as spent mostly as an offensive coordinator.
ULM Warhawks.oc: Jesse Montalto, the Iowa Central Community College head coach, in an outside-the-box hire.
ULM Warhawks.oc_status: New — the guide records Vincent giving up the coordinator role and hiring Montalto, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
ULM Warhawks.dc_status: The guide states this two ways — see the conflicts field. The team pages (pp. 336–337) record Earnest Hill entering year three as coordinator, while the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
ULM Warhawks.play_caller: Changed, and the guide treats the change as encouraging in itself: Vincent is giving up the coordinator role to better oversee the programme, and it argues too many young and first-time head coaches take on too much and cannot properly manage the rest of the job.
ULM Warhawks.offensive_scheme: Not named, but its central feature is identified: the quarterback run. The guide records Montalto's Iowa Central offense ranking fifth in the NJCAA at 38.6 points per game and fourth at 445.8 yards, with ICCC's Damarcus Creecy leading the team with 723 rushing yards at 5.5 per carry.
ULM Warhawks.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records no season above 25 sacks in about a decade, with the last two years the only ones in recent memory allowing under six yards per play.
ULM Warhawks.tempo: Expected to increase — the guide refers to a faster offense needing the defense to help it stay off the field.
ULM Warhawks.run_pass: Expected to shift toward quarterback running, and the guide measures the incumbents against that standard: Aidan Armenta posted a 12-to-8 ratio but only 57 net yards on 60 carries, while backup Landon Graves had 40 pass attempts and 14 rushes.
ULM Warhawks.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide expects dual-threat former Houston quarterback Austin Carlisle to play a lot, and supplies the backstory — ULM originally offered Carlisle as a three-star freshman in Vincent's first year at the school, so his arrival now is treated as purposeful.
ULM Warhawks.continuity: Head coach and quarterback return; the offensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 0 and 4, plus 1 for 8 returning starters, totalling 9. The team pages describe the defensive coordinator position differently — see the conflicts field.
ULM Warhawks.staff_turnover: Structural rather than wholesale: the head coach handed off the offense he had been calling, and hired a junior-college head coach to run it.
ULM Warhawks.prior_school: Iowa Central Community College for Montalto. Houston for quarterback Austin Carlisle, whom ULM had offered years earlier.
ULM Warhawks.portal_recruiting: Addressed at quarterback and on defense, where the guide records some JUCO transfers alongside returning contributors.
ULM Warhawks.vsin_assessment: Pressure applied to the coach's own specialism, with one decision credited. The guide starts from a genuine high point — Vincent brought instant legitimacy in 2024 with a 5-1 start including upset wins over UAB, Troy and James Madison — then puts the pressure squarely on his background: a career spent mostly as an offensive coordinator, yet ULM has scored 21 and 16.6 points per game in his two years, and he needs to find some offense or his tenure could be coming to a close. It calls the decision to give up play-calling encouraging. It also documents a three-year in-season pattern — 3-1 then losing every game, 5-1 in 2024 then losing every game, 2-0 in 2023 including an outright upset of Army then 10 straight losses — and offers possible causes without committing: heat and humidity in Monroe early, depth as a definite factor, or a staff that does not adjust well once opponents have them on film.
ULM Warhawks.strengths: A head coach who has already produced upset wins over UAB, Troy and James Madison, a decision to delegate play-calling that the guide credits, a coordinator hire from one of the most productive junior-college offenses with a clear quarterback-run identity, a returning quarterback plus a purposefully recruited dual-threat addition, and a defensive coordinator entering year three with his top two tacklers back.
ULM Warhawks.concerns: Two seasons averaging 21 and 16.6 points per game under an offensive-minded head coach, a defense with no season above 25 sacks in about a decade and only nine takeaways, and a documented pattern of collapsing after early-season starts in each of the last three years.
ULM Warhawks.betting: The guide's projections call for exactly 3.00 wins and make ULM an underdog in every game. Its coaching-linked market observation is the seasonal pattern — it answers 'maybe' to whether to play on ULM early and fade them late, noting the team plays its best football in September and early October before falling away completely, with a staff that may not adjust well once opponents have them on film named as one possible cause.
ULM Warhawks.conflicts: The guide states the defensive coordinator position two ways. The team pages (pp. 336–337) record Earnest Hill entering year three as coordinator with his top two tacklers back, while the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator. Both are reproduced as printed and neither is corrected.
